# Stereofold

> Stereofold is a plugin for Claude Code, Claude Science, and Codex. It puts a protein structure in a WebXR headset in real stereo depth, and the agent changes the scene when you ask: cut it open, recolor a chain, bring the binding pocket closer, measure between two parts, or load another structure without pairing again. Claude and Codex can share one session. Tested on a Quest 2 and in the visionOS simulator, not on a Vision Pro device.

## What Stereofold is

Stereofold packages two Mol* views in one plugin that speaks the Model Context
Protocol and runs on your Mac. Ask the agent host to inspect a PDB
entry and the molecular inspector opens: linked sequence selection, colors,
labels, transparency, depth cutaways, slow object rotation, and independent
movement of the molecule and the viewpoint. A separate stereo viewer renders one
image per eye. The agent can also open the structure in a WebXR headset browser and change
its scene there on request.

## Headset demos

Ask for a demo by name. In Claude Science, set up the connector once (see
Install), run `node plugin/dist/headset-host.mjs 4HHB` from the clone in a Mac
terminal, put the headset on, and ask: "Join the Stereofold scene on this Mac
and open the kinesin-walk demo." In Claude Code or Codex, ask: "Open the
kinesin-walk demo on my Quest."

- `kinesin-walk`: two kinesin heads trade the lead along a microtubule, 8.2 nm
  per step, then rest with both heads bound. PDB 5SYF, 9L7M, 8RHB, 1BG2, 3KIN.
- `atp-synthase-rotor`: the gamma stalk and a ring of ten c subunits turn under
  the catalytic head of ATP synthase, in three 120° steps per turn. PDB 6N2Y,
  6N2Z, 6N30.
- `hemoglobin-switch`: one alpha-beta pair of hemoglobin turns 14 degrees
  against the other into the R state, with O2 on every heme, then turns back.
  PDB 2DN2, 2DN1.
- `microtubule-growth`: say "grow it" and the next tier replaces the last: one
  tubulin, a dimer, a strand, then a wall three strands wide. PDB 5SYF.
- `crispr-cas9`: Cas9 with its guide RNA and both DNA strands; nine chapters
  name the guide, the PAM, the recognition lobe and the nucleases. PDB 9KJ6.
- `telomerase-haca`: the RNA-protein lobe of human telomerase, nine proteins on
  one RNA anchored by two dyskerin copies. PDB 8OUE.
- `spike`: the SARS-CoV-2 spike trimer, closed, turned on its long axis and
  shown as a surface. PDB 6VXX.
- `nucleosome`: 147 base pairs of DNA wrapped not quite twice around eight
  histones, then cut open to the core. PDB 1KX5.
- `daraxonrasib`: KRAS G12D and cyclophilin A held together by the drug, with
  its two contacts measured at 3.38 Å and 2.90 Å. PDB 9AX6.

The three moving demos have more stages: `flipbook` and `cycle` for
`kinesin-walk`, `flipbook` and `figure` for the other two. Coordinates download
from RCSB on first use and must match the digest in `plugin/demos/index.json`.
`plugin/demos/README.md` lists every demo and stage.

## Browser demo

The project page at https://jvogan.github.io/stereofold/ runs a browser demo of
crambin (PDB 1CRN). The demo needs no install, agent, or headset. It loads the
structure on request, switches between cartoon and ball-and-stick, links residue
selection between the 3D view and the sequence, and pauses rendering when it is
hidden. With the plugin, the agent makes changes like these when you ask.

## Stereo modes

Without a headset, the stereo viewer shows depth on an ordinary screen. It
renders a separate image for each eye, and the desktop viewing mode sets how
those two images appear.

Parallel view places the left-eye image on the left and the right-eye image on
the right. An observer fuses the pair by relaxing their eyes past the screen.
Stereofold letterboxes the pair so one eye is never wider than 63 mm at the
measured display density.

Cross-eye view is the same pair with the two images exchanged. An observer
fuses it by crossing their eyes instead.

Anaglyph combines both eye images through color filters, for red-cyan glasses.
Two compositors are selectable. The balanced default sends each filter only
Rec.709 luma, scaled so both eyes emit the same luma. The Dubois color
projector keeps more hue and gives the two eyes measurably unequal brightness,
so it is always an explicit choice.

Motion defaults to a slow rock, which shows depth before an observer has fused
the pair. When the system requests reduced motion, the viewer starts with no
motion. Motion can also be set to none, spin, or mouse parallax.

Eye separation is derived from an angular disparity budget and the live camera
distance, not from a fixed world-unit constant. The build carries numeric
geometry checks. Those are implementation tests, not evidence about glasses,
display crosstalk, or human stereo perception.

## Install

The source repository is https://github.com/jvogan/stereofold. Every host needs
Node.js 22 or newer. The built server is committed, so there is no build step.

Codex:

    codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/jvogan/stereofold
    codex plugin add stereofold@stereofold

Claude Code:

    claude plugin marketplace add jvogan/stereofold
    claude plugin install stereofold@stereofold

For Claude Science, use Settings → Connectors → Add connector → Local command
with absolute Node and `plugin/dist/server.mjs` paths. Add skills through
Settings → Skills. The README covers environment and sandbox settings. For the
headset, run `node plugin/dist/headset-host.mjs 4HHB` from the clone in a Mac
terminal (add `--vision-pro` for Vision Pro), then ask Claude Science to join
the Stereofold scene on this Mac. Other MCP hosts can register the same stdio
server, preserving existing entries.

Then start a new conversation and ask the host:

    Inspect PDB 1CRN in Stereofold.

## With the plugin

Ask for a PDB ID or local mmCIF file; obtain AlphaFold coordinates through your
source tools when needed. A compatible MCP Apps host can show an inspection
panel. When a panel is absent or a card does not mount, ask to open the same
inspector in a browser and verify that connection's rendered scene:

    Inspect PDB 1CRN in Stereofold and open it in my browser.

Ask the agent to recolor chains, highlight residues, or start a guided tour. The
inspector bundles ten guided tours.

To put the structure on a Meta Quest on the same Wi-Fi, ask:

    Open this structure on my Quest.

Your Mac opens Meta's Web Launch page in a browser signed in to the headset's
Meta account. Press Open there. With both devices on the same Wi-Fi, Quest
Browser loads the structure from your Mac, with no developer mode or USB cable.
Accept the certificate warning for your Mac's address and tap Enter VR. Then
keep asking in the conversation, by typing or dictating; the assistant checks
that each change renders on the headset. With headset voice set up, you can hold A or X on a controller and ask from inside the headset; this
Mac transcribes the speech. Quest 2 physical observations inform its measured limits. Other models use
capability checks and actual frame times. The quickstart at
https://github.com/jvogan/stereofold/blob/main/plugin/QUICKSTART.md gives every
step.

On Apple Vision Pro, ask the agent to open the structure on your Vision Pro.
The Mac copies a one-time link; paste it into Safari on the headset, accept
the certificate warning, and tap Enter VR. The simulator exercised an opaque session; probe the physical browser's available modes.
Stereofold has exercised this route in the visionOS 27 simulator, not on a
physical Vision Pro. The README gives the wearer steps.

For another headset browser, use `open_companion` with `connection: "lan"`,
`headset: "auto"`, and `launch: "none"`, then open the private HTTPS address
and pair through the connection dialog. The companion probes WebXR modes and
input sources, prefers passthrough when available, and falls back to opaque VR.
A launch shortcut or prior device test is not a pairing prerequisite. Simulator
checks cannot establish physical passthrough, comfort, or perceived scale.

## Standalone lessons

Copy the complete `plugin/skills/molecular-presentation/` folder, including
scripts and assets, into your host's configured skill directory. Claude Code
reads project `.claude/skills/` and personal `~/.claude/skills/`; Codex commonly
reads `~/.codex/skills/`; Claude Science supports upload and
GitHub import through Settings → Skills.

The Node 22 planner creates and compiles lesson files without a viewer or MCP
server. Live desktop chapters use the separate Molecular Structure Viewer;
headset playback uses the full Stereofold plugin. Compilation records planned
scene changes. Live application and movie rendering need their own viewer
validation and completion receipts.

## Privacy

The privacy page at https://jvogan.github.io/stereofold/privacy.html covers
agent-host data flows, voice routes, pairing credentials, local storage,
retention controls, and GitHub Pages hosting. Jacob Vogan publishes Stereofold.

Stereofold runs on your own machine. There is no hosted Stereofold service and
no account.

Stereofold connects to other hosts only in the cases that the README's Privacy
section lists. The main ones follow. Each coordinate fetch reveals your IP
address and what you asked for to the host that serves it:

- A PDB ID: RCSB (`files.rcsb.org`).
- An AlphaFold model: EMBL-EBI (`alphafold.ebi.ac.uk`).
- An `https` URL you give: the host in that URL.
- A lesson stage that is not cached: RCSB, or EMDB (`ftp.ebi.ac.uk`) for the
  one stage that uses a density map.

Putting a structure on a Quest adds Meta Web Launch: this Mac opens
`https://www.oculus.com/open_url/`, and Meta receives the page address, which is
this Mac's private Wi-Fi address, and the one-time pairing code when the launch
includes it. **Send using Meta** relays the page and the coordinates through a
Cloudflare quick tunnel. **Connect over Wi-Fi** uses no relay. The inspector's
optional **Talk** route, off until you configure an OAuth helper, sends each
recording to OpenAI for transcription.

The viewer bundles its own assets, so it needs no content delivery network at
runtime. Stereofold sends no runtime telemetry to its publisher.

## Support and terms

Support instructions are at https://jvogan.github.io/stereofold/support.html.
Report reproducible problems through the public GitHub issue tracker without
private files, recordings, credentials, or complete viewer links.

The existing MIT license and third-party terms are described at
https://jvogan.github.io/stereofold/terms.html. The repository's complete license
text remains authoritative. The project provides community support without a
guaranteed response time.

## Build from source

Node.js 22 or newer, pnpm 11.19.0, and Python 3. From the repository root:

    pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    pnpm --filter stereo-structure build
    pnpm --filter stereo-structure test
    pnpm --filter stereo-structure release

`build` rewrites the committed `plugin/dist/`, including `plugin/dist/server.mjs`
and the viewer assets. The stored inspector HTML and CSS companion are
reassembled into an inline page at runtime. `release` stages a self-contained plugin
directory and verifies it by launching the copy.

## Citation

Stereofold renders through Mol*. Cite the Mol* paper:

Sehnal D. et al. Mol* Viewer: modern web app for 3D visualization and analysis
of large biomolecular structures. Nucleic Acids Research, 2021.
doi:10.1093/nar/gkab314

The browser demo loads a local copy of the public 1CRN mmCIF file retrieved from
RCSB PDB on September 7, 2026. Crambin was deposited by W. A. Hendrickson and
M. M. Teeter. Full provenance, third-party notices, and font licenses are at
https://jvogan.github.io/stereofold/credits.html.
